newsitem.title: BELGIUM: More records for Belgian shares but U.S. data loom.
newsitem.headline: More records for Belgian shares but U.S. data loom.

text.p: Belgian shares notched up fresh records on Thursday, failing by a whisker to crack the key 2,100-point resistance level, but the inevitable was due to happen on Friday unless U.S. data spoiled the party.
The Bel-20 index closed 0.54 percent or 11.28 points higher at a closing high of 2,098.91 after earlier touching 2,102.23. Some 2.8 billion francs worth of Belgian shares were traded.
The index profited handsomely from a firmer start on Wall Street, firm bonds and dollar and gains on neighbouring markets.
But the prospect of key data in the U.S. was making players nervous -- to a certain extent.
One analyst said the market was waiting for Friday's data on January PPI, industrial production and capacity utilisation and business inventories.
"But actually, whether they're good or bad, does not make much difference any more. The market goes up anyhow," he said.
Oil firm Petrofina jumped 2.9 percent to 12,275 francs.
Dealers said it was boosted by news from Royal Dutch/Shell Group earlier on Thursday that it had record annual profits.
"People are now also expecting a strong earnings from Petrofina," one said.
Dollar-sensitive retailer Delhaize, the main gainer on Wednesday, had to settle for a modest 0.5 percent rise this time and ended at 2,045 francs.
But analysts wondered why the share was not affected more by the recent slide of its U.S. unit Food Lion.
"It (Food Lion) has lost about 20 percent in the past four weeks and still it does not have a major impact," one said.
He said that steel wire and cord maker Bekaert, which jumped 3.7 percent, had been lagging the market and was now catching up.
